title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
data_curation: Not a primary focus, but the paper relies on two pairwise preference datasets: Anthropic's HH-RLHF (helpful/harmless dialogues) and Binarized UltraFeedback (~61k instances). Instances are filtered out where chosen equals rejected, or where either response is empty; prompts longer than 1024 tokens are dropped, and sequences are truncated/padded to 1024 tokens (HH-RLHF) or 2048 tokens (UltraFeedback). Mistral-ORPO-β additionally uses Argilla's cleaned ultrafeedback-binarized-preferences-cleaned variant, demonstrating that data quality yields further gains (~91% AlpacaEval1.0 / 12.20% AlpacaEval2.0) at similar dataset size. Separate reward models are trained for one epoch: OPT-350M (RM-350M, used for PPO) and OPT-1.3B (RM-1.3B, used only to evaluate generations).
curriculum: ORPO's central design point is collapsing the standard alignment pipeline. Instead of the usual pretrain -> SFT warm-up -> preference alignment (RLHF/PPO or DPO) sequence, which needs a frozen reference SFT model and a separate warm-up stage, ORPO performs SFT and preference alignment in a single monolithic training run with no reference model. Baselines follow the conventional ordering: one epoch of SFT on chosen responses, then DPO (β=0.1, 3 epochs, best by eval loss) or PPO (per Table 5 hyperparameters). ORPO instead trains for up to 10 epochs (best by eval loss) with a single learning rate (8e-6) and a λ weighting the odds-ratio term, removing the staged curriculum entirely.
method: ORPO (Odds Ratio Preference Optimization) is a reference-free, monolithic preference alignment algorithm. Its objective is L_ORPO = E[L_SFT + λ·L_OR], where L_SFT is the standard causal-LM negative log-likelihood on chosen responses and L_OR = -log σ(log(odds(yw|x)/odds(yl|x))) with odds(y|x)=P(y|x)/(1-P(y|x)). The log-sigmoid-wrapped log odds ratio penalizes disfavored responses relative to favored ones during SFT. The gradient factors into δ(d) (a penalty that accelerates updates when the model favors the rejected response) and h(d) (a weighted contrast whose 1/(1-P) denominators amplify gradients when likelihood is low). Because no reference model is needed, ORPO halves forward passes per batch (2 vs 4) and removes the SFT warm-up. The paper argues odds ratio is preferable to probability ratio here: it is milder and avoids over-suppressing rejected-token logits before domain adaptation. λ is tuned per model (0.1 Mistral, 0.2 Llama-2, 0.25 Phi-2).
eval_metrics: Benchmarks and metrics: AlpacaEval1.0 and AlpacaEval2.0 (GPT-4 / GPT-4-turbo as judge, win rate vs text-davinci-003 and vs GPT-4), MT-Bench (GPT-4 judge, multi-turn, category scores), IFEval (instruction-following, prompt/instruction and strict/loose accuracies), reward-model win rate against SFT/PPO/DPO using RM-1.3B, and lexical diversity via Gemini-Pro embeddings (per-input and across-input average cosine similarity). Headline numbers: Mistral-ORPO-β (7B) scores 12.20% AlpacaEval2.0, 7.32 MT-Bench, 66.19% IFEval instruction-level loose; Mistral-ORPO-α (7B) scores 11.33% AlpacaEval2.0, 7.23 MT-Bench, 61.63% IFEval inst-loose. Llama-2+ORPO reaches 9.44% AlpacaEval2.0; Phi-2+ORPO 6.35%. Win-rate peaks vs SFT 80.5%, vs PPO 85.8%, vs DPO 70.9% (HH-RLHF, OPT-1.3B).
key_results: Mistral-ORPO-β (7B): 12.20% AlpacaEval2.0, 7.32 MT-Bench, 66.19% IFEval instruction-level loose—surpassing Zephyr-β and Llama-2-Chat (13B) with single-epoch training on UltraFeedback alone. ORPO win rate vs DPO reached 70.9% at OPT-1.3B scale on HH-RLHF, with the margin over DPO growing as model size increases from 125M to 1.3B and up to 7B.
evolution_note: ORPO builds on DPO's reference-free spirit (Rafailov 2023) and the unlikelihood-training tradition, reacting against the unstable multi-stage SFT->RLHF/PPO pipeline and the cost of keeping a frozen reference model. In 2024 it helped popularize single-stage, reference-free alignment and data-quality-focused preference tuning, motivating later monolithic alignment recipes that further reduce the alignment footprint.
